question: what happens when the new admission rule is applied to the episodes already executed

variance_block.refusal: no measured usage; compliance cannot be shown

pilot_block.refusal: no measured usage; compliance cannot be shown

decision_not_to_exempt: the historical blocks are not grandfathered; the rule is applied to them and the consequence is reported
why_this_does_not_retract_the_reported_w: those blocks were always labelled instrument evidence and no score or effect was ever claimed from them, and judged scoring was already inadmissible pending calibration, so the rule supplies a second independent reason rather than overturning a claim
what_it_does_change: the variance components and the allocation and minimum detectable effect derived from them are design-planning inputs taken from episodes that would not be admitted under the current rule; they are therefore labelled provisional and the confirmatory block must re-derive them from admissible episodes with measured usage
consequence_for_the_confirmatory_block: every confirmatory episode must be executed in structured output mode so its usage is measured, otherwise it cannot be scored

gate_finding.issue: one upstream archive stores its sections under an internal directory named paper, so the receipt listed member names that looked like repository paths and did not resolve
gate_finding.resolution: tex_files are now recorded as repository-relative paths under the extraction directory, which both removes the false reference and makes every listed file checkable; all listed files resolve
